style: Style: an original illustration in the manner of an 18th-century Siamese manuscript painting (samut khoi folding book) and Ayutthaya-era temple mural line art: fine black ink contour lines, flat areas of a few natural pigments only (red ochre, indigo, muted green, touches of gold leaf, chalk white), on warm aged khoi-paper texture with soft stains. Head-and-shoulders bust, three-quarter view, centred, facing slightly left, dignified and respectful. Plain aged-paper background fading to the edges, no scenery. Historically plausible late-18th-century Siamese dress and hairstyle (short-cropped mahat-thai hair). Not photorealistic, not anime, not a game character. No text, no letters, no seals, no signature, no border.

items.taksin_a: Phraya Tak (later King Taksin) at about 33, a Siamese general of Thai-Chinese (Teochew) descent: lean, determined face, calm resolute eyes, short-cropped hair, thin moustache; wearing a fitted long-sleeved Siamese noble's military jacket with a gold-trimmed collar over a dark sash, a sword hilt at the shoulder.
